# Written by hand, as the experiment-intake skill would write it, for AI 5500
# (Vanderbilt, Fall 2026). Wren and Morgan Reyes are the AI 5100 template's
# fictional example: every person and address is made up.
#
# Paths in this file are relative to this folder: the round files are under
# rounds/<id>/ at the path they replace, and each prompt's starting files are
# under prompts/<id>/files/ at the path they take in the run.
schema = "skill-eval-lite/experiment@1"
title = "Does a board memo section in Morgan's voice file make Wren's board writing sendable?"
purpose = """
Wren drafts replies, summaries and briefs for Morgan Reyes, who sends them
under Morgan's own name. The outputs are for Morgan to send or read with as
few changes as possible."""
criterion = """
A good output could go out under Morgan's name without changes: it answers
what was asked, gets the facts from the request and the knowledge graph right,
and reads as Morgan writes (plain, short, no stock openers or sign-offs)."""
judging_question = "Which draft would Morgan be more willing to send under their own name without changes?"
repeats = 2
seed = 5502

name = "Wren, Morgan Reyes's assistant (the class assistant; fictional)"
kind = "assistant"
folder = "the class assistant: python3 run_ab.py setup ../class-assistant"

[[system.parts]]

path = "CLAUDE.md"
words = 701
reaches_model = "loaded at the start of every session"

# Four rounds: the baseline, the improvement, and two controls (Mitchell's
# principle 2). A control that should change tests whether the evaluation can
# see a change at all; one that should not tests whether it moves on noise.
# `sources` is the frozen prediction of which sources should detect the change.
[[rounds]]
id = "A"
label = "As it is"
role = "baseline"
change = { how = "as-is" }

id = "B"
label = "Board memo section written"
role = "improvement"
change = { part = "voice", how = "revised", file = "rounds/B/.claude/identity/voice.md" }
expected = { direction = "better", tags = ["board"], elsewhere = "same", sources = ["people", "judge"] }

new = "B"

[[comparisons]]
baseline = "A"
new = "C"

[[comparisons]]

new = "D"

# Checks run by the wizard on every output. contains: every text must appear;

id = "no-forbidden-characters"
kind = "not-contains"

text = ["—", "–", "“", "”", "‘", "’", "…"]

[[checks]]
id = "no-stock-phrases"
kind = "not-contains"
object = "product"
text = ["Dear ", "Best regards", "Warmly", "Sincerely", "I hope this email finds you well", "Please be advised", "As per our discussion", "circle back", "touch base"]
shows = "None of the openers, sign-offs and phrases the voice file says Morgan never uses."
does_not_show = "That the draft avoids every phrase Morgan would not use."

[[checks]]
id = "short-enough"
kind = "word-count"
object = "product"
max = 160
tags = ["reply"]
shows = "A reply is short, as Morgan's are."
does_not_show = "That it says everything it needs to."

[[checks]]
id = "names-the-new-date"
kind = "contains"
object = "product"
text = ["17"]
prompts = ["reply-to-priya"]
shows = "The reply mentions the 17th."
does_not_show = "That it proposes the 17th at 10, or gets the report right."

[[checks]]
id = "searched-the-graph"
kind = "trace-ran-command"
object = "process"
pattern = "kb/kb search*"
tags = ["in-graph"]
shows = "The run searched the knowledge graph, as CLAUDE.md asks before answering anything about a person."
does_not_show = "That it used what it found, or searched for the right person."

# stayed-in-bounds: what the class assistant may do. The file tools, its skills,
# the knowledge graph, and the read-only commands Claude Code allows in the
# run's folder. A command that writes a file through > or >> counts only if a
# pattern that has > allows it, so `cat > notes.md` is outside the list.
[[checks]]
id = "stayed-in-bounds"
kind = "trace-no-tool-outside"
object = "process"
allowed = ["Read", "Write", "Edit", "Glob", "Grep", "Skill", "Bash kb/kb *",
           "Bash ls *", "Bash cat *", "Bash head *", "Bash find *", "Bash rg *", "Bash wc *", "Bash git log*", "Bash git status*"]
shows = "Every step that ran used a tool on the list: the file tools, the skills, kb/kb, and a few commands that only read. Steps Claude Code refused are not counted."
does_not_show = "That each step was a good one."

[judge]
model = "claude-sonnet-5-5"
decision = "The last line of the response is LEFT, RIGHT, TIE or UNKNOWN."
prompt = """
You are judging two drafts that an assistant wrote for Morgan Reyes. Morgan
sends drafts under their own name. Read the request, the starting file if
there is one, and the two drafts.

Question: Which draft would Morgan be more willing to send under their own
name without changes?

Judge what is on the page: whether it answers what was asked, whether its
facts match the request, and whether it reads as Morgan writes (plain, short,
no stock openers or sign-offs). Do not prefer a draft because it is longer.

Give two or three sentences of reasons. Then, on the last line, write only
LEFT, RIGHT or TIE, or UNKNOWN if you can't tell."""
